content.text:
1. The Generator Collapse (Age 9–10)
• A neighborhood makeshift generator burns out during a storm.
• Rex repairs it instinctively before adults arrive.
• Realizes he sees mechanical flow the way others see emotion.

2. The School System Failure (Pre-teens)
• Detroit school tech repeatedly breaks.
• Rex runs unofficial repair sessions for teachers and students.
• Learns:
  - leadership without authority
  - explaining under pressure
  
3. The First Big Loss (Early teens)
• A community mentor dies unexpectedly.
• Rex withdraws, then channels grief into:
  - precision
  - control
  - making broken things work again
• Sets emotional baseline: “If I can’t save people, I can save what they depend on.”

4. Engineering Program Acceleration (Teens)
• Accepted early into a young-engineers initiative.
• Gains attention from Singapore’s Technarch recruitment pipeline.
• Fascinated by high-tech precision and its ethical edge.

V. TRANSITION TO SINGAPORE
• Receives scholarship for elite engineering training.
• Moves alone at 18–19.
• Cultures of Detroit and Singapore collide:
  - Detroit = improvisation, community, resilience
  - Singapore = perfection, hierarchy, controlled innovation

This clash shapes his moral compass.

VI. SINGAPORE YEARS — SHAPING OF HIS CONSCIENCE

Professional path:
• Specializes in:
  - system stability under unpredictable load
  - tech failure modes
  - interference-resistant networks
• Draws Technarch attention for:
  - unusual intuition with fragile systems
  - ethical insistence on user safety

Moral friction:
• Rex questions Hardliner protocols early.
• Witnesses:
  - secrecy
  - impossible deadlines
  - disregard for human factors
• Refuses to join restricted-access programs (Lattice, Enforcement, Interface).
• Earns respect from Softliners, suspicion from Hardliners.

Key emotional insight:
• Technology amplifies human intent.
• Without ethics, engineering becomes harm.

VII. DEPARTURE FROM SINGAPORE
Trigger events:
• Leak of internal notes about override systems.
• A near-miss incident involving technologists (possibly involving proto-metas).

Rex decides:
• “I will not build machines that can’t care who they hurt.”
• Leaves Singapore under strained, quietly monitored circumstances.

VIII. MOVE TO NEW ORLEANS
• Drawn to the U.S. South for:
  - emotional humanity

• Calm, ethical, deeply protective
• Resistant to certainty rhetoric

Failure Modes
• Overwork
• Self-neglect
• Reluctance to delegate
• Tendency to carry responsibility alone

Saga Function
• Technical grounding for Concord
• Moral counterweight to Technarc Hardliners
• Anchor for Kade during Loom fracture
• Proof that technology reflects human intent, not destiny

Relationship Anchors
• Seraphine: trusts her judgment implicitly
• Caro: shared emergency competence
• Elisabet: clarity partnership
• Lucien: mutual respect for structure
• Tahl: ethical alignment in truth work
• Kade: post-Neon anchor and stabilizer
• Lacuna: shared understanding of fragile systems

Resonance Rule
• Not metaphysical
• Sensitive to resonance only through system failure and distortion
• Never channels or amplifies resonance

Endgame Constraint
• Cannot ascend
• Must remain human-scale
• Survives by choosing care over control

REX — 7-BUNDLE CHARACTER VISUAL CANON
Wiry · Precise · Practical · Quietly Protective
============================================================

# BUNDLE 1 — SILHOUETTE & BODY PROPORTIONS

## 1.1 Height & Build
- Height: **5'10"–5'11"**
- Build Tier: **Wiry-Functional (Athletic C)**
- Weight distribution: lean core, long forearms, defined but modest musculature
- Overall impression: **practical strength**, compact readiness, field-engineer utility

## 1.2 Posture Grammar
- Baseline: slightly forward-leaning, ready-to-move posture  
- Shoulders: relaxed but alert, subtle hunch from years of benchwork  
- Emotional openness: shoulders broaden, face softens, eyes steady  
- Stress posture: neck tightens, shoulders rise, hands hover near tools  
- Comfort posture: weight shifts to one leg, arms fold loosely, small half-smile

## 1.3 Movement Vocabulary
- Motion is **controlled, efficient, tool-minded**
- Walk: quick, purposeful steps; eyes scan environment while moving  
- Gesture:
  - taps fingers against thigh or toolbelt  
  - checks imaginary readouts during problem-solving  
  - wipes palms on pants when nervous  
- Forbidden: swagger, grand gestures, theatricality, performative dominance

## 1.4 Trilogy Silhouette Evolution
- **Veil:** civilian-functional; engineer silhouette with clean lines  
- **Neon:** resopunk repair layering; stress-wear; teal-grid flickers on edges  
- **Loom:** hardened survival silhouette; multi-pocket techwear; storm-rated layers  
- **Post-Mending:** simplified, heirloom repairs; soft teal accents; grounded clarity

============================================================

# BUNDLE 2 — FACE, HAIR & EXPRESSION GRAMMAR

## 2.1 Facial Structure
- Sharp, thoughtful features  
- High, straight nose; defined jawline  
- Eyes: warm brown or hazel with analytical sharpness  
- Brows: expressive; knit together during concentration  
- Mouth: subtle expressions; quick micro-smiles  
- Overall impression: perceptive, grounded, quietly intense

## 2.2 Hair
- Short to medium length, often pushed back or finger-combed  
- Texture: straight to slight wave  
- Stress tell: runs hand through hair repeatedly  
- Era styling:
  - Veil: casual short cut  
  - Neon: grown out slightly, pushed back from work intensity  
  - Loom: practical trimming, weather-ready  
  - Post-Mending: relaxed, slightly longer, softened edges

## 2.3 Expression Grammar
- Resting: focused, mild furrow in brow  
- Thinking: lips purse slightly, brow deepens, head tilts  
- Emotional: eye-softening, micro-smile, breath shift  
- Stress: jaw tightens, eyes flick rapidly as if scanning  
- Forbidden: exaggerated grimaces, melodramatic anguish, anime-wide eyes

============================================================

# BUNDLE 3 — RESONANCE BEHAVIOR & VFX

## 3.1 Color & Light
- Baseline: **teal-blue grid flicker**, subtle diagnostic shimmer
